technology.summary: Today's technology news includes the announcement of Microsoft's new AI chip, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. Amazon has over 1 million robot workers, which raises questions about the future of human employees. A former Plaud executive has raised $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background. The Fitbit Edge fitness tracker has been officially announced, and Apple's "Welcome Home" event is expected to bring updates to Apple TV and HomePod Mini, as well as a new smart home hub.

finance.summary: Today's most important finance news includes the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India joining forces to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. The Nifty 50 index closed down by 95.75 points, reaching 22,620.45, due to profit booking and rising oil prices. The BSE Hospitals Index faced a steep 5% drop after the Supreme Court of India urged a probe into reports of patients being directed to specific pharmacies for their medications. A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt.

politics.summary:
The Delhi High Court has dismissed pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence. The Supreme Court will list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar, where protesters are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a Mumbai protest were detained and threatened with police cases.

In other news, Donald Trump has cited a non-existent Indian election to call the US electoral process 'corrupt'. Jairam Ramesh has attacked the CEC, saying his ability to execute illegal orders makes him a liability for the country. India's foreign exchange reserves have dropped by $18.34 billion in a single week.

Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
